title: Change file permissions using text method
summary: Use chmod with letters (u, g, o, a) and symbols (r, w, x) to grant or remove specific permissions for the owner, group, or others.

steps.explain: Set permissions for a specific user class. Replace <WHO> with u (user), g (group), o (others), or a (all). Replace <PERMS> with combinations of r, w, x, or leave empty to remove all.

placeholders.name: WHO
placeholders.description: Who to change: u (owner), g (group), o (others), a (all).

placeholders.name: PERMS
placeholders.description: Permissions to set: r (read), w (write), x (execute). Empty string removes all.

placeholders.name: FILENAME
placeholders.description: Path to the file or directory.

alternatives.explain: Add a permission without removing others.

placeholders.name: WHO
placeholders.description: Who to change: u, g, o, a.

placeholders.name: PERM
placeholders.description: Single permission to add: r, w, or x.

alternatives.explain: Remove a permission without affecting others.

placeholders.name: WHO
placeholders.description: Who to change: u, g, o, a.

placeholders.name: PERM
placeholders.description: Single permission to remove: r, w, or x.

rollback.explain: Restore original permissions if known, or use numeric method if you know the original octal value.

warnings: Changing permissions incorrectly can lock you out of files or expose sensitive data.
Always verify the current permissions with 'ls -l' before changing them.
